translations.en: Wooden barrels are indispensable when making liquor, aren't they?
We owe them so much.
When you leave liquor to age in a barrel,
flavor seeps out of the wood, and the liquor takes on color.
The longer it ages,
the more things keep seeping out of the barrel.
Yet when it's sold, it's transferred to glass bottles.
Why is that? Why, I wonder?
And so, here's my question.
Which is better for storing liquor for a hundred years?
Leave it in the barrel, or transfer it to a glass bottle?
Leave it in the barrel
Transfer it to a glass bottle
Very good. Leave it in the barrel, then.
